summary:
Project description

Ember Drift is a browser-based arcade flight game in which you pilot a rocket through a series of increasingly demanding levels. Each level asks you to collect energy shards while managing a limited energy meter, so every boost and maneuver has a cost. You can choose from several rockets, each with different handling, and unlock new skins and medium settings as you play. Mid-run ability picks add tactical variety, and a daily challenge gives players a reason to return. The game runs entirely in the browser with no installation, and it includes a leaderboard for tracking high scores.
details:
Ember Drift is a browser space-flight game built as a single HTML file with no installation needed. The player pilots a small rocket through a star field where each star has its own gravitational pull. Flying with the arrow keys or WASD on a computer, or a joystick and pulse button on a phone, the player collects energy shards to meet each level’s target while dodging asteroids, satellite parts, and space junk. A pulse burst, charged by holding a button, lets the player thrust in the direction they face, which turns each star’s pull into a skill test. Chaining shards builds a combo multiplier that raises the score. Random event waves such as meteor showers, junk storms, and shard rain keep runs unpredictable. The game has five levels, each with its own color palette and rising difficulty. After level 4, the player picks one ability (shield, time slow, or magnet) for the final level. Players also unlock rocket types, ship skins, and gravity settings, plus a daily challenge that changes each day. Scores are saved on the device, and on the published page they feed a shared leaderboard.

It was built with plain JavaScript and the HTML canvas API, with CSS for the interface. All sound and music are generated in real time with the Web Audio API, so the game loads without any audio files. It uses the Vibration API for haptic feedback on supported phones and adjusts its layout for left- or right-handed phone play. The project’s creative focus is the gravity-driven flight and the procedurally generated music, which speeds up and adds layers as levels and danger increase. We designed it to be quick to start and easy to pick up, while the later levels and abilities reward mastery. Its intended impact is to give players a short, engaging challenge they can play anywhere.
